nodes.name: Warn Channel (Outlook)
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Microsoft Outlook — recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.

nodes.name: Page Urgently (Slack)

Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Archive Unscored
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Event Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Merge Tier Outcomes
nodes.notes: Rejoins 4 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

# Notify stakeholders on changes with Outlook

**Pattern:** Event Notification · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers escalations work end to end across Outlook, Google Sheets and Slack.

It moves through 10 working steps, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Read Metrics from Outlook
3. Compute Severity Signals
4. Grade Severity Tier
5. Just Record (Info)
6. Warn Channel (Outlook)
7. Page Urgently (Slack)
8. Archive Unscored
9. Merge Tier Outcomes
10. Send Summary to Outlook

## Why it exists

Doing escalations work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Read Metrics from Outlook → Compute Severity Signals → Grade Severity Tier → Just Record (Info) → Warn Channel (Outlook) → Page Urgently (Slack) → Archive Unscored → Merge Tier Outcomes → Send Summary to Outlook

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Outlook and Google Sheets aligned by hand for escalations
- Pushing escalations events into Outlook and Google Sheets the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Escalations work where "Read Metrics from Outlook" is still a manual step before Outlook
- Escalations work that only reaches Outlook when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Outlook and Google Sheets in step for escalations, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Outlook or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 10 nodes in this escalations build
- Branches rejoin before Outlook, so a escalations run reports once rather than 10 times
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for escalations
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 10 nodes for escalations before wiring Outlook

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Three response tiers, not a single yes/no alert, match the response to the severity — logging every metric quietly would bury the one critical spike, and paging on-call for every info-level blip trains them to ignore alerts entirely. Critical gets a distinct, louder channel from warning on purpose.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Adjust the tier thresholds and see how alert sensitivity changes.
2. Trigger a critical-tier value and confirm it pages a different channel than warning does.
3. Add a 4th tier between warning and critical.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole escalations payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your escalations process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
